summary: This photo-essay profiles local environmental stewards who protect urban parks through volunteer work, education, technology, and clean-up efforts. Each section covers a different person or group, from invasive species removal to water quality testing and digital mapping. Together they show a network of dedicated individuals sustaining the city's green spaces.
one_line: A photo-essay profiling volunteer stewards who protect city parks through invasive species removal, education, digital mapping, waterway cleanup, and tending green spaces.
key_facts: Martha Jensen, a retired biology teacher, formed the Green Shield Brigade three years ago; the group was met at Redwood Park on September 7, 2023.
The Green Shield Brigade monitors park flora, combats invasive species, and keeps walking paths and recreational areas clean.
Thomas "Tommy" McAllister, a botanist, leads a weekend volunteer corps removing invasive species; on October 12, 2023 he was clearing Himalayan blackberry in Willow Creek Park.
McAllister compared invasive species removal to "playing whack-a-mole," saying "every cleared area is a victory for the native plants and creatures that rely on them."
Jessica Alvarez, an environmental education coordinator, oversees the "Seeds of Change" initiative at Grand Oak Community Park, observed September 25, 2023.
Seeds of Change brings students from local schools into parks to learn ecology and conservation; students plant saplings and analyze water samples.
School groups under Alvarez's guidance have reintroduced native plant species to several park areas.
Raj Patel, a software engineer with GIS expertise, leads the Digital Defenders at Hendricks Valley Nature Preserve, mapping since late September 2023.
The Digital Defenders' maps track erosion patterns and plot locations of rare plant species to help park authorities set maintenance and conservation priorities.
Victor Nguyen, a hydrologist, leads the Waterway Warriors at Fairview River Park, whose efforts started in earnest on October 6, 2023.
The Waterway Warriors conduct regular water quality tests and clean-up campaigns and educate the public about pollutants' impact on aquatic ecosystems.
Linda Santiago tends flower beds and a fledgling oak at Tanglewood Commons and connects with hundreds who share her passion for nature.
